metadata.title: Build Landing Page with Value Proposition

story.iWant: to immediately understand what this tool does when I arrive
story.soThat: I can start using it without confusion
story.tasks:
- Task 1: Create main page component structure (AC: 1) - Create `/app/page.tsx` as client component with `"use client"` directive - Add semantic HTML structure: ``, ``, `` elements - Import necessary Shadcn UI components (Button, Input, Card) - Set up React state hooks for location input, loading, answer data, error states
- Task 2: Implement landing page header and value proposition (AC: 1) - Add H1 heading with text "Will It Rain?" - Style H1 with large, prominent typography using Tailwind CSS - Add subheading with text "Get a simple yes or no answer for the next 24 hours" - Use Shadcn UI typography patterns for consistent styling - Center content with generous white space (mobile-first approach)
- Task 3: Add location input field placeholder (AC: 1) - Import Shadcn UI Input component - Create controlled input with placeholder "Enter zipcode or city" - Position input prominently below value proposition - Add proper ARIA labels for accessibility - Add focus management for keyboard users - Note: Full validation and submission logic deferred to Story 3.2
- Task 4: Create footer with privacy statement and attribution (AC: 1) - Add footer element at bottom of page - Include privacy statement: "We don't store your location or search history" - Add OpenWeather attribution: "Weather data provided by OpenWeather" - Use subtle typography (smaller font size, muted color) - Ensure footer is visible but doesn't distract from main content
- Task 5: Implement responsive design (AC: 1) - Use Tailwind CSS mobile-first breakpoints (sm:, md:, lg:) - Test layout on mobile (320px-767px): single-column, centered - Test layout on tablet (768px-1024px): centered with comfortable spacing - Test layout on desktop (1025px+): centered content with max-width constraint - Ensure text is readable without zooming (minimum 16px base font) - Verify no horizontal scrolling at any breakpoint
- Task 6: Add SEO meta tags and basic PWA metadata (AC: 1) - Update `app/page.tsx` with metadata export (Next.js 15 pattern) - Set page title: "Will It Rain? | Simple 24-Hour Rain Forecast" - Add meta description: "Get a simple yes or no answer about rain in your area for the next 24 hours" - Verify PWA manifest metadata from Story 1.4 is still active - Add Open Graph tags for social sharing (optional enhancement)
- Task 7: Manual testing and validation (AC: 1) - Test landing page loads without errors (`npm run dev`) - Verify H1 and subheading display correctly - Verify input field is visible and accessible (placeholder text visible) - Verify footer displays privacy statement and attribution - Test responsive design on Chrome DevTools (mobile, tablet, desktop) - Test keyboard accessibility: Tab to input, focus indicators visible - TypeScript compilation passes (`npm run type-check`) - ESLint validation passes (`npm run lint`) - Lighthouse audit: Accessibility > 95

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. **Given** a user visits the app for the first time **When** the landing page loads **Then** the H1 heading displays "Will It Rain?" **And** a clear subheading explains: "Get a simple yes or no answer for the next 24 hours" **And** the location input field is prominently visible and accessible **And** the page uses clean, minimal design with Shadcn UI components **And** a footer includes privacy statement and OpenWeather attribution **And** the page is fully responsive (mobile, tablet, desktop)

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Simple Answer Experience
doc.snippet: Frontend architecture using Next.js App Router with app/page.tsx as primary file. Uses React useState hooks for state management, Tailwind CSS v4 with Shadcn UI components (Button, Input, Card). All interactive elements require "use client" directive.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Simple Answer Experience
doc.snippet: H1 heading "Will It Rain?" prominently displayed, subheading "Get a simple yes or no answer for the next 24 hours", location input field centered and accessible, footer with privacy statement and OpenWeather attribution, responsive on mobile/tablet/desktop.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Simple Answer Experience
doc.snippet: All interactive elements keyboard accessible (Tab, Enter), semantic HTML (h1, main, form, button, label), form inputs have associated labels, loading states use aria-live="polite", error messages use aria-live="assertive", focus indicators visible.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Simple Answer Experience
doc.snippet: Mobile (320px-767px): single-column layout, touch-optimized. Tablet (768px-1024px): centered layout, comfortable spacing. Desktop (1025px+): centered content, max-width constraint. Text readable without zooming (16px base), touch targets 44x44px, no horizontal scrolling.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Simple Answer Experience
doc.snippet: All frontend dependencies installed in Epic 1. No new dependencies required. Shadcn UI components (Button, Input, Card) already available. TypeScript types from Epic 2 available for reuse (types/api.ts, types/weather.ts).

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Simple Answer Experience
doc.snippet: Manual browser testing on localhost:3000. No automated unit tests (deferred to Epic 5). TypeScript validation (npm run type-check), ESLint validation (npm run lint), Lighthouse audit for accessibility and performance. Test responsive design on Chrome DevTools.

constraints.constraint: Use Next.js 15 App Router pattern - page.tsx must be a client component with "use client" directive for interactive elements
Import Shadcn UI components from @/components/ui/* - Button, Input, Card components are available
Use TypeScript strict mode - no any types, proper typing for all props and state
Mobile-first responsive design - use Tailwind breakpoints sm:, md:, lg: for responsive layout
Semantic HTML structure - use header, main, footer elements for accessibility
Add ARIA labels and keyboard navigation support - all interactive elements must be accessible
Minimum 16px base font size for readability without zooming
Test with TypeScript compilation (npm run type-check) and ESLint (npm run lint)
Follow code quality standards from Epic 2 - comprehensive JSDoc comments, clear error handling
Do NOT implement API integration yet - deferred to Story 3.2 and 3.9

tests.standards: Manual browser testing is the primary approach for Epic 3. Start development server (npm run dev), test on http://localhost:3000. Run TypeScript validation (npm run type-check) and ESLint validation (npm run lint). Use Lighthouse audit in Chrome DevTools for accessibility and performance scores (targets: Accessibility > 95, Performance > 90). Test responsive design using Chrome DevTools device emulation. No automated unit tests required for Epic 3 (deferred to Epic 5).
tests.locations: N/A - No automated test files for Epic 3. Manual testing only.

ideas.idea: Test landing page loads without errors by running npm run dev and navigating to http://localhost:3000. Verify no console errors appear.
Verify H1 heading displays "Will It Rain?" with large, prominent typography. Check font size and visual hierarchy.
Verify subheading displays "Get a simple yes or no answer for the next 24 hours" with appropriate styling. Check text color and size.
Verify location input field is visible with placeholder text "Enter zipcode or city". Test that input accepts keyboard input.
Verify footer displays privacy statement "We don't store your location or search history" and OpenWeather attribution "Weather data provided by OpenWeather".
Test responsive design on Chrome DevTools: Mobile (320px), Tablet (768px), Desktop (1024px+). Verify single-column layout on mobile, centered layout on larger screens.
Test keyboard accessibility: Press Tab key to move focus to input field. Verify focus indicator (ring) is visible.
Run npm run type-check to verify TypeScript compilation passes with zero errors.
Run npm run lint to verify ESLint validation passes with zero errors.
Run Lighthouse audit in Chrome DevTools. Verify Accessibility score > 95 and Performance score > 90.
